title: Netherlands – Microscopes – Confocal Microscope
description: The objective of this Procurement Procedure is for Radboud University Medical Center (Radboudumc) to select and contract a single Contractor for the supply, installation, commissioning, training, and maintenance of a Confocal Microscope System for use by RTC Light Microscopy. Through this procurement, Radboudumc intends to expand its existing microscopy infrastructure with a user-friendly and future-proof system capable of delivering rapid, high-resolution three-dimensional (3D) imaging. The intended system shall support the current and future research needs of Radboudumc and contribute to maintaining a state-of-the-art microscopy facility. The microscope system will be installed as a shared research facility within RTC Light Microscopy and will be centrally managed by the UMC. Following installation, commissioning, and the completion of the required user training, the system will be made available to authorised and qualified Radboudumc staff and researchers. The Contracting Authority seeks a reliable and sustainable solution that combines high imaging performance with ease of use, operational continuity, and long-term support throughout the lifecycle of the system.

title: JSOW AGM-154C Initial Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) and Training for Taiwan Air Force (TAF)
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Patuxent River, MD awarded a Delivery Order under Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N0001925G0009 to Raytheon Company, 1151 E. Hermans Road, Tucson, AZ 85756-9367 for Joint Standoff Weapon (JSOW) AGM-154C Initial Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) and Training for Taiwan Air Force (TAF) F-16 Block 20. This acquisition was pursued on a sole source basis under the statutory authority of Title 10, U.S.C. title: Custodial Services at Altus AFB
description: POSTAWARD NOTICE Solicitation FA441926Q0002 was posted via SAM.gov on 2 July 2026. A total of twenty-four (24) quotes were received in response to FA441926Q0002. Below is the award information: a. Contractor: MAGADIA CONSULTING, INC. b. Award Date: 20 November 26 c. Contract Number: FA441926D0002 d. Total Evaluated Price: $ 4,475,979.42 e. Technical Rating: Acceptable f. Past Performance Confidence Rating: Recent � Very Relevant -Substantial Confidence g. Decision Summary: Pricing has been determined fair and reasonable. As a result, IDIQ Contract FA441927D0002 with a TEP of $4,475,979.42 and a contract ceiling of $9,000,000.00 will be awarded to Magadia Consulting, Inc. (CAGE: 59SC7 / UEI: PJDZNFZVJJ87). An initial Task Order will be issued concurrently with basic contract award to obligate the guaranteed minimum contract minimum of $60,000.00. 3. As stated in �Attachment 4 � Evaluation Factors� The evaluation will begin with a cursory review of all submissions for completeness. If an offeror fails to submit a complete submission, including a complete SF 1449, bid schedule, technical volume, and past performance records, the offeror will be rendered non-responsive, and no further evaluation will be conducted. The evaluation team will rank complete quotes by Total Evaluated Price (TEP) from lowest to highest (see below detailed explanation on the calculation of TEP). The evaluation will begin by evaluating the technical submissions of the three (3) lowest ranked quotes. If the technical submissions of the three (3) lowest ranked offers are acceptable, the evaluation process will proceed to the next step. If any of the three (3) lowest ranked offers results in an unacceptable rating, the evaluation team will evaluate the next lowest offeror, as initially ranked TEP, for technical acceptability. Evaluation at this step will continue until there are three (3) technically acceptable offerors. The three (3) lowest priced, technically acceptable, responsive offers will then be evaluated for past performance. If these offers do not yield at least two (2) offerors with an overall rating of Substantial or Satisfactory Confidence, the evaluation process will continue until a minimum of two (2) offerors with an overall rating of Substantial or Satisfactory Confidence are identified or all quotes are evaluated. The Source Selection Authority shall then make an integrated assessment to render the best value award decision. The Source Selection Authority may also make the determination that it is in the best interest of the Government to evaluate all offerors for technical acceptability and past performance prior to rendering the best value award decision. While the Government will strive for maximum objectivity, the acquisition process, by its nature, is subjective; and therefore, professional judgment is implicit throughout the entire process. Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to all required terms and conditions, includes all required representations and certifications, meets all requirements set forth in the solicitation and provides the best value to the Government. The submission ranked first (1st) based on Factor 1was found to be non-responsive and was removed from competition. The submissions ranked second (2nd), third (3rd) and fourth (4th) based on Factor 1: Price all received Technical Rating: Acceptable based on the criteria in Factor 2. All three were then evaluated for Past Performance using the criteria outlined in Factor 3. All three were found to be recent and relevant. The evaluation determined one (1) offer to be Satisfactory Confidence, one (1) offer to be Neutral Confidence and one (1) to be Substantial Confidence. Magadia Consulting Inc. was determined to be the responsible offeror whose quote represents the best value, defined as providing the greatest confidence that the vendor will satisfy the Government's requirements affordably.

title: 48--MANIFOLD ASSEMBLY P
TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: PBI High-Temperature Hollow Fiber Membranes
description: Polybenzimidazole (PBI) High-Temperature Hollow Fiber Membranes offer a practical way to improve separation efficiency in process environments where standard polymer membranes often lose performance or durability. The platform combines high-temperature operation, chemical resistance and compact hollow-fiber design in a membrane system that can help users recover hydrogen, separate carbon dioxide and process difficult liquid streams with lower energy demand and a smaller equipment footprint than many conventional approaches. Because the fibers are formed from a robust PBI material and engineered with an integrated thin selective layer, the technology is well suited for organizations seeking stronger performance in demanding energy, chemical and water treatment settings. How it Works The membrane works like a selective gate built into a very small hollow strand. A mixed gas or liquid flows across the fiber, and the thin outer layer allows some molecules to pass through more readily than others, while the porous support beneath it gives the fiber strength and a path for transport. The disclosed fabrication process forms that selective layer and support structure in one step, then can add heat treatment or a thin sealing layer to improve stability and sharpen separation performance. Technical Description The polybenzimidazole invention is centered on a method for making asymmetric hollow fiber membranes from polybenzimidazole, a polymer valued for strong thermal and chemical stability. A PBI dope solution and a bore fluid are extruded through a spinneret, then passed through an optional air gap and into a water coagulation bath, which forms a hollow fiber with an integrated selective layer and a porous support structure. The process can produce nearly defect-free selective layers, and the patent states that selective layer thickness can be controlled from about 0.1 to 5 �m, with examples demonstrating thicknesses down to about 160 nm and one example near 0.38 �m. A major technical advantage is control over membrane microstructure and durability. PBI High-Temperature Hollow Fiber Membranes emphasize macrovoid-free fibers, which are important because macrovoids create weak points that can fail under high temperature and pressure. The membranes can be thermally annealed or chemically crosslinked to improve solvent resistance and stability, and a defect-sealing layer can be added to improve selectivity without changing the core fiber architecture. In demonstrated gas-separation modules, the technology showed hydrogen permeance above 100 GPU, with one example reporting 242 GPU at 250 �C and hydrogen/carbon dioxide selectivity of 19.1, while long-term testing in wet syngas with 20 ppm H2S showed stable performance over 40 days. The patent also states that the membranes can operate up to about 400 �C and are suitable for gas, vapor and liquid separations including hydrogen purification, carbon capture, brine treatment and organic solvent separations. Advantages Operates at temperatures that are too demanding for many conventional polymer membranes Resists harsh chemical exposure including steam and sulfur-containing gases compact module design enables smaller equipment footprint easier scaling than ceramic membranes higher throughput without compromising permeability, selectivity or membrane area cost Combines selectivity and structural support in one integrated membrane architecture Supports both gas and liquid separation opportunities across multiple industries Reduces overall hydrogen purification costs Has already been tested in relevant operating environments rather than remaining only a laboratory concept Market Applications Energy and Power generation (hydrogen production, pre-combustion carbon capture, syngas cleanup) Oil and Gas (refining, natural gas processing, produced water treatment) Chemical and Petrochemical Processing (process gas separation, solvent dehydration, feedstream cleanup) Industrial Water and Wastewater (high-salinity brines, water purification, water and acid separation) Advanced Fuels (Fischer-Tropsch processing, fuel conversion, synthesis gas upgrading) Specialty Manufacturing (organic solvent recovery, pharmaceutical and fine chemical separations) Development Status: TRL 5 US Patent No. 10,071,345 LA-UR-26-24561 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. title: V225--VA AIR AMBULANCE BROKER WITH SUPPORTING GROUND TRANSPORTATION VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY NOTICE
description: VA AIR AMBULANCE BROKER WITH SUPPORTING GROUND TRANSPORTATION VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY NOTICE December 10-11, 2026 Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veterans Transportation Program (VTP) Network Contracting Office (NCO) 20 1. Purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Transportation Program (VTP), will host an Industry Day to engage with air and ground transportation brokers capable of providing Air Ambulance Broker with Supporting Ground Transportation Services nationwide. This Industry Day is not a request for proposal. It is a market research tool being used to determine potential firms capable of providing the services described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition. The purpose of this session is to: Provide industry with an overview of the upcoming Air Ambulance Broker Services requirement. Offer vendors an opportunity to ask questions and provide feedback prior to release of the solicitation. Support industry�s understanding of VTP�s operational needs, compliance requirements, and contracting expectations as defined within the Performance Work Statement (PWS). 2. Requirement Overview The upcoming procurement will establish multiple-award IDIQ contracts for nationwide fixed-wing and rotary-wing air ambulance broker services, supported by ancillary ground transportation services which refers to transportation services used to transport Veterans between airports, healthcare facilities, Veterans' residences, and other approved destinations. Ground transportation modes may include private vehicles, taxis, rideshare services, wheelchair-accessible vans and shuttles, ambulances, and other specialized transportation services necessary to meet a Veteran's mobility, accessibility, or medical transportation needs. Key highlights include: 24/7/365 availability including holidays Compliance with CAMTS/NAAMTA transport standards Real-time communication and documentation via VA Mandated Transportation Software Quality Control and subcontractor oversight requirements Support for advanced life support, life support, basic life support, critical care transport and stretcher transports 3. The Request for Proposal The Request for Proposal number is 36C26027R0012. The solicitation will result in the award of three (3) to five (5) firm fixed-price MATOCs. The applicable NAICS code is 481211, Nonscheduled Chartered Passenger Air Transportation with a small business size standard of 1,500 employees. 4. Industry Day will be held virtually, on Microsoft Teams, on December 10 � 11, 2026. A hybrid format for this Industry Day is anticipated: December 10, 2026 Morning Session: General overview for all prospective offerors Afternoon Sessions: Optional one-on-one discussions with individual vendors (NTE 50 minutes) December 11, 2026 All Day: Optional one-on-one discussions with individual vendors (NTE 50 minutes hour) Please note that all times for the scheduled sessions will be stated in Pacific Standard Time (PST) 5. Points of Contact (POCs) Contracting (NCO 20): Primary: Wendy Duval @ wendy.duval@va.gov Alternates: Michael Allred @ michael.allred1@va.gov Program Office (VTP): Primary: Tony Guagliardo Alternate: Mindy LaCrone 6. Tentative Agenda Welcome & Introductions Overview of VTP Mission and Needs Air Ambulance PWS Requirements Review Acquisition Strategy & Timeline Vendor Q&A One-on-one Sessions with Interested Offerors 7. Additional Notices This Industry Day is informational only and does not constitute a solicitation or request for proposals. Draft documentation, including the PWS and/or the RFP, may be provided for industry review prior to or during the session. 8. Registration Instructions It is suggested that prime contractors that have both the capabilities and relevant experience to perform most of the required tasks participate. Significant subcontractors may also participate. Interested parties should provide a short (10 Pages) capability statement to the above Contracting POC with the following information: Company Name, Unique Entity ID number (SAM.gov), business size and classification, address and point of contact with phone number & e-mail address. Address your firm's ability to provide nationwide Air Ambulance Broker Services, including fixed-wing, rotary-wing, and ancillary ground transportation services. Describe your process for subcontractor oversight, accreditation status, dispatch and operational capabilities, relevant federal experience providing similar services. Indicate whether attending general session only or requesting a one?on?one breakout Submit any initial questions you may have to help shape agenda topics and ensure the VA has sufficient time to fully answer questions.

description: This notice is issued solely for market research and planning. It is not a solicitation, request for proposal, invitation for bid, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. title: eFOIA
description: The Air Force is seeking innovative commercial solutions to modernize, streamline, and replace its legacy Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) infrastructure. This Call is issued under the authority of the overarching Department of the Air Force (DAF) Program Acquisition Executive (PAE) Business and Enterprise Systems (BES) Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) to identify, evaluate, and acquire an Electronic FOIA (eFOIA) Technology System capable of managing the absolute end-to-end lifecycle of a FOIA request. The objective of this Call is to pilot and scale a secure, cloud-native implementation with the ability to host in Cloud One (Government hosted) and carry out a highly automated software solution that dramatically reduces backlog, speeds up response times, ensures strict compliance with ever-changing federal regulations including a secure cyber posture, and provides an intuitive interface for both agency personnel and public requesters.

description: This Area of Interest (AOI) is issued under the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Rapid Infrastructure for Science and Experimentation ('RISE') parent notice FA8652279-RISE pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Refer to the attached AOI document and attachments for submission instructions, technical requirements, and assessment criteria. To optimize the work environment and facility functionality for personnel in the 2nd Floor hallway of Building 556, Acquisition Management Complex, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio. This project transforms an existing standard entrance hallway into a modern, motivating environment that reinforces the strategic deterrence mission and heritage of the USAF Bombers community through bomber-specific environmental wall graphics, heraldry shields, structural scale models, historical elements, painting, architectural finishes, decals, and visual enhancement using existing space and structures. Target Timeline: The entire project must be completed within ninety (90) calendar days of award: Stage 1 Design Plan (30 days), Stage 2 Sourcing & Fabrication (60 days), and Stage 3 Physical Implementation & Closeout (90 days). title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – EÜ Kieler Str.: L1 OPL EÜ/LSW, TWP, OPL VA Gleis; L2 OPL VA Str., SVK, Leitungspl.// 1-4 üb.;5-7opt.
description: Die EÜ Kieler Straße in Hamburg (Strecke 1234, km 1,809) muss saniert, teilerneuert oder erneuert werden. Das denkmalgeschützte Bestandsbauwerk wurde 1927 errichtet und basiert auf einer stählernen Rahmenkonstruktion. Das Bauwerk überführt die Güterumgehungsbahn (Strecke 1234) über die Kieler Straße (B 4) mit zwei Fahrstreifen sowie beidseitigen Fuß- und Radwegen. Bei der letzten Prüfung und Instandsetzung 2024/25 wurden massive Schäden am Bauwerk festgestellt. Die Restnutzungsdauer ist laut Prüfbericht des EBA-Prüfsachverständigen nur unter Auflagen bis Ende 06/2029 gewährleistet. Bis dahin muss die Brücke saniert, ertüchtigt oder durch einen Neubau oder eine Hilfsbrücke ersetzt werden. Die EÜ steht unter Denkmalschutz und ist daher grundsätzlich zu erhalten. Nur wenn eine denkmalgerechte Sanierung nachweislich nicht möglich ist, kann die EÜ teilerneuert oder erneuert werden. Die Sanierungsfähigkeit wird in einer gesonderten Machbarkeitsstudie untersucht, die nicht Bestandteil dieses Vergabevorgangs ist. Auf dieser Grundlage wird in der Vorplanung im Variantenvergleich festgelegt, ob das Bauwerk saniert, teil- oder ganz erneuert wird. Zentrale Planungsaufgabe ist die Aufweitung der lichten Höhe von 4,00 m auf 4,50 m durch Anhebung der Gleisgradiente, Absenkung der Straße oder eine Kombination aus beidem. Bahnlinks befindet sich eine 2,00 m ü. SO hohe Lärmschutzwand. Im Bauwerksbereich wird sie auf einem separat gegründeten Torsionsbalken geführt und ist im Zuge der Planungsaufgabe mit zu beplanen. Die Planungsleistungen (LPH 1 bis 4, optional LPH 5 bis 7) werden ohne BIM-Methodik in zwei Losen vergeben: Los 1 „EÜ Kieler Straße“: Objektplanung Ingenieurbauwerke (EÜ sowie Torsionsbalken mit Lärmschutzwand), Tragwerksplanung Ingenieurbauwerke, Objektplanung Verkehrsanlagen (Gleisanlage/Oberbau). Los 2 „Straßenverkehrskonzept“: Objektplanung Verkehrsanlagen (Straßenanlage), Erstellung eines Straßenverkehrskonzepts, Leitungstrassenplanung im Straßenraum.

Deze ruwe terreinen vereisen gespecialiseerde voertuigen alle terrein om de manschappen, benodigde materiaal en vereiste bluswater ter plaatse te krijgen. Hulpverleningszone Noord-Limburg beschikt reeds over bosbrandvoertuigen type CCF en wil haar vloot uitbreiden met 2 bijkomende bosbrandvoertuigen type CCF 4x4 4.000 l, één voor de nieuwe brandweerpost Peer en één voor brandweerpost Lommel. Beide voertuigen zijn identiek. Het voertuig van brandweerpost Peer dient echter bijkomend uitgerust te worden met een sproeibalk en een systeem voor de dosering van zeep/detergent zodat dit voertuig buiten de winterperiode eveneens gebruikt kan worden voor kleine opdrachten “reinigen wegdek”. In het dossier zal eveneens een bepakkingslijst toegevoegd worden. De aanbieder dient hiervoor de eenheidsprijzen op te geven zodat i.f.v. het resterende budget het voertuig bijkomend uitgerust kan worden met brandbestrijdingsmaterialen. Overige materialen zullen door de Hulpverleningszone Noord-Limburg aangeleverd worden zodat de nodige ruimte voorzien kan worden tijdens de opbouw. De uniformiteit van inrichting van deze nieuwe voertuigen t.o.v. de reeds in gebruik zijnde CCF’s dient behouden te blijven (in samenspraak met de Hulpverleningszone tijdens de opbouw/inrichting). Al het voorgestelde materieel dient nieuw te zijn en elk element dient te voldoen aan de bijzondere interventievoorwaarden. De leverancier dient hiermee rekening te houden bij het voorstellen van het materieel. Het voertuig betreft een bosbrandwagen type CCF voor 4 personen. Het voertuig dient voorzien te zijn van een autoprotectiesysteem met een gereserveerde hoeveelheid water om in geval van nood de bemanning te kunnen beschermen. Het chassis moet van een goedgekeurd en gehomologeerd type zijn, aangepast aan het voertuigontwerp. Deze aanpassing wordt onderbouwd door een gewichtsberekening van het volledige concept, die bij de offerte wordt gevoegd. Bij levering zal het voertuig worden nagewogen. Indien het voertuig niet voldoet aan het vooropgestelde gewicht, kan dit aanleiding geven tot weigering van het product. Het aangeboden voertuig moet van het meest recente commerciële type zijn en geschikt zijn voor rijden en inzet op ruw terrein (oneffenheden in terrein, bospaden, losse zand, heuvels,…). Het voertuig moet op het moment van indiening van de offerte én bij levering volledig voldoen aan de geldende Europese en Belgische regelgeving.

title: POLYSERP Antivenom (ACAN)
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT The Department of National Defence (DND), through the Strategic Medical Countermeasures Program (SMCP) on behalf of the Canadian Forces Health Services Group (CF H Svcs Gp), has a requirement for the supply of POLYSERP MENA and POLYSERP PAN-AFRICA snake antivenoms for the treatment of cytotoxic, hemotoxic, and neurotoxic snakebite envenomation syndromes caused by multiple snake species. The required products must consist of broad-spectrum snake antivenoms suitable for the treatment of envenomation caused by medically important snake species encountered in Sub-Saharan Africa, North Africa, and the Middle East. The products must provide equivalent geographic and species coverage across the required deployment regions and meet all applicable regulatory, quality assurance, packaging, labelling, and shelf-life requirements specified in the solicitation documents. The initial requirement consists of the supply of 36 vials of POLYSERP MENA and 36 vials of POLYSERP PAN-AFRICA for delivery no later than 31 March 2027. The resulting contract is anticipated to be valid from contract award date to 31 March 2031 and includes additional scheduled deliveries of 36 vials of POLYSERP MENA and 36 vials of POLYSERP PAN-AFRICA in Fiscal Year 2028-2029 and 36 vials of POLYSERP MENA and 36 vials of POLYSERP PAN-AFRICA in Fiscal Year 2030-2031. The contract will also include an option for up to an additional 72 vials of POLYSERP MENA and 72 vials of POLYSERP PAN-AFRICA exercisable during the contract period. This procurement will be conducted through an Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN). The Government of Canada has identified CRO, LLC as the only supplier currently known to satisfy the operational, clinical and technical requirements associated with this requirement. Market research identified alternative regional antivenom products; however, none were found to meet the mandatory requirement for equivalent broad-spectrum geographic and species coverage across the required deployment regions. Suppliers that consider themselves fully qualified and capable of meeting the complete requirement may submit a Statement of Capabilities during the posting period. The Crown retains the rights to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Barring any applicable trade agreement exceptions or other legal restrictions, eligible suppliers may participate in this solicitation process. Applicable trade agreements are being invoked under the corresponding Limited Tendering provisions. NOTE TO SUPPLIERS: Procurement Assistance Canada offers seminars to businesses interested in learning how to sell goods and services to the Government of Canada. These seminars are provided free of charge.

title: Natural Resources Conservation Program Technical Support Services - Camp Darby, Italy
description: Natural Resources Conservation Program Technical Support Services -U.S. Army Garrison Italy, Darby Military Community (DMC), Livorno, Italy 1. Notice Type and Purpose This is a Sources Sought Notice issued by the Department of War (DoW), U.S. Army Garrison Italy, Darby Military Community (DMC), for market-research and acquisition-planning purposes only. The Government is seeking information from capable and interested businesses that can provide non-personal natural-resources conservation program technical support services for DMC in Livorno, Italy. This notice is not a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, invitation for bid, or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not pay for preparation of responses or reimburse any costs incurred in responding to this notice. Responses will be used solely to conduct market research, assess the availability of qualified sources, support acquisition planning, evaluate potential small-business participation, refine the anticipated scope, evaluate industry interest in an Industry Engagement Day, and determine the final acquisition strategy. The Government seeks responses from all responsible business concerns, including small businesses and businesses participating in applicable socioeconomic programs. 2. Anticipated Requirement The Government is conducting market research to identify firms capable of providing qualified personnel, technical expertise, supervision, transportation, equipment, supplies, and incidental services necessary to provide natural-resources conservation technical support. The anticipated requirement will include on-site and field-based technical support for natural-resources surveys, monitoring, technical analyses, field data collection, technical reporting, forestry, forest nursery and greenhouse operations, mitigation and compensatory projects, landscape assessments, Valutazione d�Incidenza Ambientale (VIncA) and SIncA development, wolf monitoring, pine tortoise scale technical support, regulatory technical support, and Geographic Information System (GIS) support. The final scope, workload, task order structure, labor categories, contract type, period of performance, and individual technical requirements remain subject to refinement after completion of market research and review of submitted capability statements. 2.1 Natural Resources Technical Support The contractor will provide technical support to the Government for natural-resources conservation activities. The contractor will perform work only in response to Government tasking and under the technical direction, review, and oversight of a designated Government employee. The contractor will: Conduct field surveys, monitoring, data collection, analysis, and preparation of draft technical reports addressing: Protected species; Habitats and protected biotopes; Wildlife and ungulate management; Wolf populations; Wetlands and water resources; Forestry and vegetation; Noxious weeds and invasive species; Pine tortoise scale infestation and related forest-health conditions; and Other natural-resources conditions identified by the Government. Monitor wolf populations at Government-designated locations and prepare draft field reports, survey data, maps, photo documentation, and technical observations for Government review. Conduct Government-directed field observation, assessment, monitoring, and technical analysis related to pine tortoise scale infestation within DMC and the Tuscany Region, as applicable. Document observed effects on pine resources and prepare draft technical summaries of Government-provided or publicly available host-nation phytosanitary requirements, regional action-plan measures, and potential natural-resources implications for Government review. Prepare draft natural-resources management plans, plan updates, technical studies, and supporting documentation for Government review. Potential products will include support to: Forest-management planning; Threatened and endangered species management planning; Wetland-management or wetland-restoration planning; Integrated Natural Resources Management Plan updates; and Other Government-identified natural-resources technical products. Prepare draft technical recommendations, field documentation, photo logs, maps, briefing materials, and other natural-resources technical products for Government review. Provide technical support during Government-led inspections, site visits, environmental reviews, and natural-resources project-planning activities. Review and analyze applicable natural-resources and environmental requirements and prepare draft technical summaries of potential implications for DMC operations, training, construction, land use, forestry, wildlife, wetlands, mitigation projects, compensatory projects, and other mission activities. Identify potential environmental, natural-resources, schedule, permit, authorization, or mission impacts associated with Government-provided project information and prepare draft technical observations and recommendations for Government review. The contractor will provide technical support only. The contractor will not perform natural-resources program administration, establish Government priorities, make program decisions, approve work, manage Government official records systems, or perform other inherently governmental functions. 2.2 Regulatory Technical Support and Mission-Impact Analysis The contractor will provide technical support to the Government by reviewing and analyzing applicable natural-resources and environmental requirements and preparing draft technical products for Government review. The contractor will demonstrate the ability to read, analyze, and assess the potential operational and natural-resources implications of applicable requirements, including, as relevant to Government tasking: Army Regulation 200-1, Environmental Protection and Enhancement. Army in Europe Regulation 200-1, Army in Europe Environmental Quality Program, as applicable. Overseas Environmental Baseline Guidance Document. Italy Final Governing Standards. Applicable U.S. Army, U.S. Army Europe, U.S. Army Garrison Italy, and DMC environmental procedures or technical guidance provided by the Government. Applicable European Union environmental directives, regulations, guidance, and protected-area requirements. Applicable Italian national, Tuscany Region, local, Park Authority, and other host-nation environmental, natural-resources, landscape, phytosanitary, protected-species, wetland, forestry, and related requirements. Government-provided permits, authorizations, agreements, management plans, VIncA conditions, mitigation conditions, compensatory-project conditions, and other relevant documents. The contractor will: Prepare draft regulatory-change summaries and issue papers. Prepare draft technical analyses of potential effects on the Army mission at DMC, including training, operations, construction, land use, forestry, natural-resources management, protected species, wetlands, mitigation projects, compensatory projects, and other mission-support activities. Prepare draft technical recommendations, implementation considerations, and proposed updates to Government technical products. Identify issues requiring Government review, legal review, environmental review, contracting review, safety review, security review, or official coordination with host-nation authorities. Support Government review of host-nation requirements related to pine tortoise scale infestation, forest-health conditions, wildlife, protected species, wetlands, forestry, landscape assessments, VIncA, SIncA, mitigation, and compensatory projects. The contractor will not provide legal opinions, make final regulatory interpretations, determine compliance, establish the applicability of a legal requirement to the Government, approve a course of action, or make official commitments to host-nation authorities. title: APN-General Safety Training Services, BC
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE General Safety Training Services British Columbia (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform consultants of an upcoming contract opportunity at various locations in British Columbia. The purpose of this APN is to allow consultants to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested [contractors and consultants] to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE Standing Offer Agreement AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN Number:88336 Approximate Estimate: $1,000,000 Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027 Description: It is the Department of National Defence/Canadian Armed Forces (DND/CAF) policy to maintain a General Safety Program (GSP), which ensures that safety considerations are incorporated into every aspect of departmental operations, training, and support activities. The Consultant will be responsible to maintain (if necessary) and deliver training courses on an as needed basis to DND/CAF in the courses falling within a General Safety training category. Safety training courses that may be requested to be delivered by the Consultant include: confined space entry and rescue; fall arrest equipment inspection; first aid training, and asbestos and lead procedures. The estimated total potential opportunity is approximately $1,000,000 over the 5-year period. 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing consultants early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, consultants that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Consultants that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Angela Dang Procurement Specialist (Operations) Defence Construction Canada 306-830-5337 Angela.dang@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: TBN ON-AIRPORT LEASED SPACE - TSA SOLE SOURCE
description: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) intends to award a sole source lease for a total of 20 years (3 years firm, seventeen, 1-year renewal periods) to the Cities of Waynesville and Saint Robert at Waynesville�St. Robert Regional Airport ("TBN"). TSA occupies 261 rentable sq. ft. of breakroom and office space in the airport terminal. This is a notice of intent to award a sole source procurement action for leased space that is currently contracted under Transportation Security Administration, Direct Leasing Branch. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. This justification applies to all TSA continuing need requirements for support and administrative work space that is required to be on airport property at TBN. TSA space must be located on-airport to effectively carry out its mission in direct airport support of the screener workforce and administration staff that supports the screener workforce and other functions located on airport property. The lease shall include limited janitorial services and utilities as part of the rental consideration, and have the ability to securely house a 24-hour operation within the space. Due to mission critical duties, the space must be accessible by major arterial roads and/ or public transportation systems to the airport. The Government may consider alternative space if economically advantageous; otherwise the Government intends to pursue a sole source acquisition. All offerors should be aware that the Government will consider the cost of relocation, alterations, etc., when deciding whether it should relocate to another in-terminal or off-site location. A determination by the Government to not compete this proposed procurement action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. TSA will not reimburse for any costs incurred by interested parties in providing a notification of interest and/or capability statement in response to this posting. To submit a location for inspection, contact this office by December 4, 2026, 09:00 am ET. (Submissions by other than the owner or manager of a property must be accompanied by a letter from the owner granting permission to make a general offering of the space.) WRITTEN EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST MUST INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: Building Name and Address, Rentable and Usable Square Footage, Fully Serviced Rental rate and Common Area Factor, proximity to airport terminals, proximity to mass transit, available parking and Building Floor plans. Interested parties should send this information in writing, via email to Charlotte.Carney1@tsa.dhs.gov by the date specified above and ensure receipt by the Government.

title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: SurfGraphPro
description: SurfGraphPro, an AI tool, transforms complex protein structures into an easy-to-analyze format that helps researchers quickly identify binding sites, predict molecular interactions and understand protein behavior with greater speed and scalability than traditional approaches. By combining 3D surface graph representations with advanced machine learning, this technology from Los Alamos National Laboratory reduces the computational burden of protein analysis while preserving the structural detail needed for high-value applications in drug discovery, antibody design, pathogen detection and custom protein engineering. The Challenge: Protein surfaces are extremely complex, three-dimensional structures, and that complexity makes them difficult to analyze using traditional computational approaches. In practice, many existing methods rely on hand-selected biochemical features, expensive calculations or narrow task-specific models that do not generalize well to new questions. As a result, researchers can face slow runtimes, limited scalability and incomplete insight when trying to identify binding sites, predict molecular interactions or understand broader protein behavior across large sets of proteins. These limitations can make it difficult to move quickly from protein structure data to useful predictions in areas such as drug discovery, antibody design, pathogen detection and protein engineering. Problems Solved: SurfGraphPro solves these problems by converting protein surfaces into a graph-based representation that preserves both the physical shape of the surface and the biochemical information carried by surface-exposed amino acids. This tool gives machine learning models a more efficient and flexible way to process protein structures without requiring repeated manual feature engineering or highly specialized analysis pipelines for each new use case. By reducing computational burden while keeping the key structural details needed for prediction, SurfGraphPro makes it possible to analyze proteins more quickly, at larger scale and across a wider range of applications. This approach includes identifying likely binding sites, estimating molecular compatibility, supporting drug screening efforts, improving antibody and protein design workflows, and enabling other protein-focused prediction tasks where speed, scalability and adaptability matter. Key Advantages: Helps turn complex protein structures into information computers can use more easily Speeds up protein analysis compared with older approaches Reduces the amount of manual feature engineering needed Preserves important details about both protein shape and chemical properties Supports multiple uses, including drug discovery, antibody design and pathogen detection Offers a flexible platform that can be adapted to different protein-related tasks Market Applications: Pharmaceuticals and Biotechnology (drug discovery, target screening, protein optimization) Biologics and Antibody Development (antibody engineering, binding analysis, therapeutic design) Diagnostics and Infectious Disease (pathogen detection, biomarker analysis, assay development) Agricultural Biotechnology (protein analysis, crop trait research, bio-based product development) Materials and Industrial Science (protein-mineral interaction studies, polymer compatibility, bio-inspired materials) Research Tools and Software (protein modeling, computational biology, prediction platforms) Development Status: TRL 3 US Patent pending LA-UR-26-23589 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. LANL�s licensing program focuses on moving inventions developed by our researchers to commercial innovations. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov. Note: This is not a call for external services for the development of this technology. https://www.lanl.gov/engage/collaboration/feynman-center/partner-with-us/licensing-technology m.lanl.gov/tech-search

title: Finland – Real estate services – Syväkeräysastioiden vuosihuollot / VAV
description: Tilaajan tavoitteena on hankkia joustava ja luotettava yhteistyökumppani Vantaalla sijaitsevien VAV-konsernin omistamien vuokratalokohteiden syväkeräysjätepisteiden vuosihuoltoihin. VAV-konserni omistaa noin 12 000 vuokra-asuntoa, joissa asuu noin 19 000 asukasta. Tarkempi luettelo sopimuksen piiriin kuuluvista syväkeräyskohteista on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevassa kohdeluettelossa. Sopimus ei sisällä määräostovelvoitetta, eikä Tilaaja sitoudu tarjouspyynnössä tai hankintailmoituksessa esitettyihin arvioihin hankintamääristä. Työtilauksiin voi sisältyä myös tarvikehankintoja ja muita työn suorittamiseen liittyviä palveluhankintoja. Tavoitteiden saavuttamisen edellytykset on kerrottu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön ESPD-lomakkeella, hankinnan kohteen kriteerit -osiossa sekä hankintailmoituksen liitteissä. Hankintapäätöksen tekoperusteena on kokonaistaloudellinen edullisuus pisteytyksen mukaisesti, jossa maksimipisteet ovat 1000 pistettä. Tarjoajan on annettava tarjous kaikista tarjouslomakkeen töistä. Mikäli Tarjoaja ei ole tarjonnut kaikkia tarjouslomakkeeseen eriteltyjä töitä, tulkitaan tarjous puutteelliseksi. Puutteellinen tarjous hylätään. Tarjoajan kannalta huomioitavaa on myös se, että tarjottujen töiden ja hintojen tulee sisältää kaikki tässä tarjouspyynnössä, hankintasopimusluonnoksessa ja palvelukuvauksessa määritellyt kriteerit. Palvelu toteutetaan tarjouspyynnön, palvelukuvauksen ja laatuvaatimusten mukaisesti. Tarjoajan antama tarjous on sitova. Hankintasopimus syntyy vasta kirjallisen sopimuksen allekirjoittamisella, selonottoneuvottelujen jälkeen. EU-kynnysarvon ylittävässä hankinnassa sopimus voidaan tehdä aikaisintaan 14 vuorokauden kuluttua siitä, kun Tarjoaja on saanut tai hänen katsotaan saaneen päätöksen perusteluineen tiedoksi. Tarjoaja ei saa esittää esimerkiksi omissa tarjousasiakirjoissaan ehtoja, jotka vaikuttaisivat hankintasopimuksen sisältöön. Sopimuskauden tavoitealkamisajankohta on 1.2.2027 ja sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi, kuuden (6) kuukauden irtisanomisajalla.
